headline: AI valuation jitters deepen into a tech-led risk-off week
body: Friday's close confirmed the week's tone rather than reversing it: the Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2.1%, the S&P 500 fell roughly 1%, and the Dow slipped a milder 0.4%, leaving the Nasdaq down near 4.5% on the week -- its worst stretch since late June -- against a comparatively modest 2% weekly loss for the S&P and a Dow that actually finished the week higher. That divergence is the clearest signal in the tape: money rotated out of the most crowded, capex-heavy AI and semiconductor names and into value and industrial-tilted names rather than fleeing equities outright. It's consistent with the credit-quality unease that hit AI-infrastructure financing earlier in the week, and with survey data showing a large share of institutional investors now naming an AI bubble as their top portfolio risk, with more than half believing AI-linked stocks are already overvalued.

Two cross-currents are complicating any read that this is purely a tech story. Brent crude pushed back toward $110 a barrel, its highest level since spring, as renewed Iranian activity around the Strait of Hormuz revived a supply-disruption premium -- an inflationary wrinkle landing right as a hotter-than-expected CPI print was already cutting into hopes for near-term Fed easing. Together those two headlines argue against a clean 'growth scare' narrative and more for a market repricing both rate-cut timing and AI-capex risk at once. Retail-sentiment chatter was thin and didn't offer a clear contrarian read today, so this take leans more on index price action, oil, and the rate/inflation data than on social-media positioning.
